Matches the subtitle («Zinazoweza Kukataa»). The verbal noun «kukataa» is used as the noun throughout («Kukataa kulikuwa nadra»); «ukataaji» avoided as less idiomatic. Conscientious objection: «kukataa utumishi wa kijeshi kwa sababu ya dhamiri».

No settled Swahili term. «msururu» (a line, a succession of things one after another) chosen for the cases passing one at a time. «mnyororo» (chain) rejected because «mnyororo wa ugavi» (supply chain) appears in the same chapter and the kill chain will need it later; «bomba» (literal pipe) reads only as plumbing or oil. Targeting pipeline: «msururu wa kulenga shabaha»; the deportation pipeline: «msururu wa utekaji nyara na uhamishaji wa kulazimishwa».
Stamps of a different sign: «mihuri ya upande wa pili».

«kijenzi» is the usual technical word for a component; «kipande» (piece) for part, because «sehemu» is taken by the book's Parts (Sehemu ya IV). Cycle time: «muda wa awamu moja» (not «mzunguko», which is the loop).

sw: utiishwaji wa kijamii; utumwa wa kimashine
note: No settled Swahili Deleuze–Guattari vocabulary. The subject (the person as subject) is «mhusika»; «kiima» (grammatical subject) rejected as grammatical. Needs a native check, ideally by a reader of Swahili philosophy.
No settled Swahili term; clearest literal rendering, with «mzunguko» (loop, cycle). Chain of command is «ngazi za uongozi», to keep «mzunguko» and «mnyororo» free.
No settled short term; this is the clearest («list of people to be killed»). Shorter alternatives such as «orodha ya mauaji» read as a list of killings.
No settled Swahili noun; «mkataaji» is the regular agent noun from «kukataa». Needs a native check.

en: peer (Milgram's defying peers; the defiant peer)
note: Plain «companion, fellow» forms; «rika» (age-mate) rejected as about age. Possessive changes with the sentence.

«Kupanga» (arrange, set up, organize) keeps the sense of deciding who is in the room; «kuunda» was kept for formation to avoid merging the two terms. Weak point: chapter 1's «Composing is a word for making» becomes «Kupanga ni neno la kutengeneza kitu», where «kupanga» is less obviously a making word than «compose». Needs a native check.
No settled Swahili term. Rendered descriptively («bias toward trusting the machine»), clearer than the calque «upendeleo wa kiotomatiki».
«modeli» as in the edition's notice («modeli ya lugha»).

Plain register: the word an adult says out loud, neither clinical nor crude. Don't make it polite. A term of labor satire, never set beside the kill chain (D-810). «Kukojoa» is the everyday verb; «kukojolea» its applicative, “to pee into”. Plainer noun form: «chupa ya mkojo» (bottle of urine). Needs a native check.
Hirschman's exit, voice: «kutoka, sauti». Literal; no Swahili edition of Hirschman known to the translator.
No settled Swahili term in machine learning; literal «uzito» (weight), emphasized in the Preface as the English emphasizes it. Needs a native check.
AI is «akili bandia» throughout. «zalishi» (productive, generating) is the coined adjective; not checked against Swahili tech press usage.
